bottom_line: Simvastatin–ezetimibe vs simvastatin monotherapy reduced the 7-year Kaplan–Meier primary composite end-point event rate (hazard ratio, 0.936; 95% confidence interval, 0.89 to 0.99).
implications: In this trial of 18,144 post–acute coronary syndrome patients, adding ezetimibe to simvastatin was associated with a lower 7-year Kaplan–Meier rate of the primary composite outcome (32.7% vs 34.7%; hazard ratio, 0.936; 95% CI, 0.89 to 0.99; P=0.016) alongside lower median time-weighted average LDL cholesterol (53.7 vs 69.5 mg per deciliter). The document also reports that prespecified muscle, gallbladder, hepatic adverse effects and cancer were similar between groups; it does not show a difference in death from cardiovascular causes (hazard ratio 1.00; 95% CI 0.89–1.13) or death from any cause (hazard ratio 0.99; 95% CI 0.91–1.07).

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized trial in 18,144 patients hospitalized for acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days.
major_points.quote: We conducted a double-blind, randomized trial involving 18,144 patients who had been hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days

major_points.text: Compared simvastatin 40 mg + ezetimibe 10 mg vs simvastatin 40 mg + placebo.
major_points.quote: The combination of simvastatin (40 mg) and ezetimibe (10 mg) (simvastatin–ezetimibe) was compared with simvastatin (40 mg) and placebo (simvastatin monotherapy).

major_points.text: Primary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, unstable angina rehospitalization, revascularization ≥30 days, or nonfatal stroke.
major_points.quote: The primary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, unstable angina requiring rehospitalization, coronary revascularization (≥30 days after randomization), or nonfatal stroke.

major_points.text: Primary end-point 7-year Kaplan–Meier event rate was 32.7% vs 34.7% (hazard ratio 0.936; 95% CI 0.89–0.99; P=0.016).
major_points.quote: The Kaplan–Meier event rate for the primary end point at 7 years was 32.7% in the simvastatin–ezetimibe group, as compared with 34.7% in the simvastatin-monotherapy group (absolute risk difference, 2.0 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.936; 95% confidence interval, 0.89 to 0.99; P = 0.016).

major_points.text: Median time-weighted average LDL cholesterol during the trial was lower with simvastatin–ezetimibe than with simvastatin monotherapy (53.7 vs 69.5 mg/dl).
major_points.quote: Over the course of the entire trial, the median time-weighted average LDL cholesterol level was 69.5 mg per deciliter (1.8 mmol per liter) in the simvastatin-monotherapy group and 53.7 mg per deciliter (1.4 mmol per liter) in the simvastatin–ezetimibe group.

major_points.text: Prespecified muscle, gallbladder, hepatic adverse effects and cancer were reported as similar between groups.
major_points.quote: Rates of prespecified muscle, gallbladder, and hepatic adverse effects and cancer were similar in the two groups.
